name: MixEval-Hard
intro: MixEval-Hard 是从论文目标为 4,000 条的 MixEval 中按模型预测结果抽取的 1,000 条困难子集。论文用错误矩阵 A（1 表示模型答错）和各模型准确率 μ 计算样本难度 ξ，再按 exp(λξ) 提高困难样本的抽取概率，并用聚类距离阈值限制分布偏移；最终样本保留源基准真值，95.22% 为英文。
org: National University of Singapore, Carnegie Mellon University, Allen Institute for AI
build_method: MixEval 模型预测矩阵, 准确率加权难度, 指数概率拒绝采样, 聚类距离分布约束
metric: 自由回答 0–1 分与选择题准确率按样本数加权的总分；Arena Elo 排名相关性仅用于跨模型元评估
eval_feature: 困难子集, 动态, 预测依赖更新
scale: 1,000 个样本（自由回答 500 + 选择题 500）
task_type_en: Multiple-choice Question Answering, Free-form Question Answering
build_method_en: MixEval model-prediction matrix, accuracy-weighted difficulty, exponential-probability rejection sampling, cluster-distance distribution constraint
intro_en: MixEval-Hard is a 1,000-item difficult subset drawn from the paper's 4,000-item MixEval target using model prediction results. The paper forms an error matrix A (1 means an incorrect model response), weights each item by model accuracies μ to obtain difficulty ξ, increases hard-item draw probability with exp(λξ), and limits distribution shift with a cluster-distance threshold. The accepted items retain source-benchmark ground truths and are 95.22% English.
metric_en: Sample-count-weighted overall score from free-form 0–1 scores and multiple-choice accuracy; Arena Elo rank correlation is across-model meta-evaluation only

drawio_review_note: Paper/source audit fixed on 2026-07-18. The primary paper is arXiv:2406.06565v2 and the reviewed PDF has SHA-256 26c94aa106bf898fa87ec4e6632136d81d879de78b2354f1b1e37c30dd450536. Sections 3.1-3.4, Figure 4, Table 1, Table 2, Section 4.1, Appendix A.5, and Appendix G were checked. MixEval-Hard inherits the complete MixEval reconstruction boundary: two detector benchmarks, prompted Vicuna-33B over a Common Crawl subset, GPT-4 positive/negative relabeling of about 20k candidates, a trained detector with over 99% recall and over 98% precision, 2M detected Common Crawl queries, GPT-4 Turbo text-in/text-out filtering, and Top-1 matching to development/test items from 18 ground-truth benchmarks with normalized all-mpnet-base-v2 dot products plus an input/context-length constraint. The paper target and fixed Hugging Face revision for source MixEval contain 4,000 items and retain source ground truths. In the fixed Git tree, release 2024-06-01 has 2,000 free-form plus 2,000 multiple-choice rows, whereas release 2024-08-11 has 2,000 plus 1,995 rows (3,995 total). Section 3.3 then defines the Hard-specific pipeline. Several models are run on MixEval to form A, a 0-1 matrix of shape N_model by N_MixEval, with 1 meaning incorrect. Each item column A_i is weighted by the vector of model accuracies μ, giving difficulty ξ_i = μ dot A_i. Candidate draw probability is proportional to exp(lambda times ξ_i), so higher-difficulty items are proposed more often. Rejection sampling accepts a candidate only while cluster distance alpha(B-double-prime union candidate, B-prime) is no greater than tau; otherwise it resamples. This makes sampling difficulty-first while constraining distribution drift relative to MixEval, which was aligned to wild queries. The accepted dataset has 1,000 items, 95.22% English, and retains source ground truths; the fixed Git data contains 500 free-form and 500 multiple-choice rows. Dynamic refresh has the same three upstream alternatives as MixEval: a different uniform web-query batch, the latest Common Crawl, or a newly expanded ground-truth benchmark pool. Hard additionally requires prediction-dependent resampling. The paper reports that MixEval updates within one minute, while MixEval-Hard update time depends on the sampling models; using GPT-4 Turbo predictions alone takes about two minutes. Five random-seed MixEval versions show score standard deviation 0.36, 99.71% unique web queries, and 85.05% unique MixEval items. Evaluation behavior was checked at official Git commit 7c52b41929d461df7733573528bdfb08774b0c53. Chat models use official or FastChat templates; base models are 5-shot. GPT-3.5-Turbo-0125 is the default model parser. Free-form responses receive a permitted 0.0-1.0 score in [[score]] form, MC responses yield an option such as [[A]], and MC grading is exact equality. Unresolved parser results are retried for 10 outer rounds; remaining free-form tasks get a random one-decimal score and MC tasks a random option. A request blocked after 10 BadRequest events becomes 0.0 for free-form and random for MC. The code fixes the random seed at 42. The leaderboard overall score is the sample-count-weighted combination of free-form and MC, whereas Arena Elo rank correlation is across-model meta-evaluation rather than per-item grading. Release/open-source boundary: the Git tree provides evaluation code and dynamic datasets but the construction code for detection, Common Crawl mining, benchmark mixing, difficulty calculation, distribution-constrained sampling, and automatic refresh is not published. The repository has no LICENSE file; setup.py contains an MIT classifier but no grant document. The pinned Hugging Face dataset revision 66a05ec3821a2b5089ed1e32a5d65ab6ecdbf906 declares apache-2.0 in its card. The benchmark is therefore marked partly public, not fully public. The official homepage provides a public leaderboard, but end-to-end reconstruction remains unreproducible from the released repository alone. Formal publication evidence [site-a11v-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 3308×1465 (English) and 3285×1465 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 3306×1463 and 3283×1463. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
